newsitem.title: ITALY: Ambroveneto/Cariplo link interesting idea - Bazoli.
newsitem.headline: Ambroveneto/Cariplo link interesting idea - Bazoli.

text.p: A possible alliance between Italian banks Ambroveneto and Cariplo has been studied by bank analysts and judged to be an interesting idea, Ambroveneto chairman Giovanni Bazoli said.

But before putting the issue to Banco Ambrosiano Veneto shareholders, it was necessary to see what the foundation which controls Cassa di Risparmio delle Provincie Lombarde decided regarding Cariplo's privatisation, Bazoli told reporters after Ambroveneto's annual shareholders meeting.

Cariplo, Italy's largest savings bank, has said it hopes for a stock market flotation this year after parliament approves a decree law reorganising the foundations which control many of the country's major banks.

There has been widespread market and press talk of a strategic link, if not a merger, between the two banks with speculation Cariplo might subscribe to a capital increase planned by Ambroveneto for later this year.
Bazoli confirmed the planned capital increase would go ahead this year.

Press reports have suggested Cariplo wants to see a strategic alliance with Ambroveneto and with the Italian stock market awash with talk of banks merging, traders say the Ambroveneto-Cariplo link-up appears one of the most likely.
"The Cariplo idea has been examined as a project of extrardinary interest, an excellent and positive one," Bazoli said, noting the "functional and territorial complementariness" of the two banks.

"It's one of the possible directions for the bank's development," Bazoli said. But until Cariplo's foundation gave details of the privatisation "there's no point in me talking about it with shareholders."
At 1320 GMT, Ambroveneto shares were off 0.74 percent at 4,140 lire on a slightly firmer Milan bourse.
